rules.title: Da Waaagh
rules.text:
Da Waaagh, the Marienburg Annual's plot for Greenskins, does not run like the other plots. Its warband gains and loses Campaign Points faster, and when its total drops below a rung it loses that rung's achievement until its total rises to it again, where the other plots keep an achievement once reached. Its Waagh level, which Da Camp's items and locations read, is the number of rungs it holds, not its total of points.

At 5 Campaign Points Da Camp opens: any Greenskin Hero, and no other, may visit it instead of searching for a rare item, and Da Prophet there gives the leader his first prophecy (the Da Prophecy charts). Each prophecy completed scores D3 Campaign Points.

The 40 rung is not a win by itself. It needs all six prophecies completed and full WAAAGH, and opens the special scenario Nice Day for a Waaagh Beheadin': winning it wins the campaign, and losing it costs the warband 2D6 Campaign Points.

rules.title: Equipment limits
rules.text:
What one warrior may carry: one piece of headgear (a helmet, circlet, skull cap or mask); one suit of armour on his body, and an undergarment such as steel cloth or Cathayan silk beneath it; two talismans (rabbit's feet, lucky charms, evaluated wyrdstone and the like); any number of miscellaneous items (rope and hooks, telescopes, maps); one cloak (a thief's cloak, a Sea Dragon cloak, an elf cloak); two close combat weapons and two missile weapons, though a warrior with extra arms, or a tail he fights with, carries one more close combat weapon for each; one ring (a scorpion, fortune or venom ring); and one pair of boots, a second pair only with two extra legs. Artefacts count towards none of these, and a warrior may carry any number of them. Where your group disagrees about what an item counts as, put it to a vote.

A large model that can take objectives, such as an ogre, or a warrior of Strength 5 or more, may carry a large objective such as a crate or barrel alone, at his normal speed but never running.

rules.title: Taking the Slayer oath
rules.text:
A Dwarf warband may play with these rules. A Dwarf who does one of the following takes a Leadership test after the game, and on a failure takes the Slayer oath: loses an item worth 200 gc or more; fails the rout test at the first attempt (the leader only); has his whole warband wiped from the board (every Dwarf Hero); loses to the same warband at least 3 times (the leader only); loses Campaign Points (the leader only); or is taken out of action by an Elf.

He misses the next D3 games while he travels to the shrine of Grimnir. A Slayer keeps all his skills and weapons, may no longer wear armour of any kind, and gains the skill Deathwish: he is immune to all psychology and never tests for fighting alone.

rules.title: Slayer titles
rules.text:
A Slayer earns each title below with its feat, and its rule with it. The rules add up: a new title never takes an old one's away. Single combat means no other friendly warrior is in base contact when the beast falls.

Large Slayer: kill a Large creature in single combat, and take its name (Minotaur Slayer, Ogre Slayer, Troll Slayer). He may wound on a 4+ instead of using his Strength.

Greater Slayer: kill a daemonic or greater undead creature in single combat, and take its name (Lich Slayer, Vampire Slayer, Pink Horror Slayer). His attacks count as magic.

Gigantic Slayer: kill a gigantic beast in single combat, one with the Great Beast rule or 5 or more Wounds, and take its name (Colossal Squig Slayer, Merwyrm Slayer). He gains Heart Strike on one dice, declared before rolling. The book never says what Heart Strike does.

rules.title: Eye of the Gods
rules.text:
Every Chaos warband in the campaign is encouraged to use the Eye of the Gods, the Marks of the Dark Gods and Gifted Servants, which the Annual reprints from Border Town Burning (p183) and Corrupted Characters.

Any Chaos warband may add 15 gc to its leader's hire cost to give him the Eye of the Gods, as the Marauders of Chaos warband has it. If he becomes a Chaos Spawn the warband may keep it, and it passes to each new leader.

rules.title: Marks of the Dark Gods
rules.text: For 10 gc more on the hire cost of a Chaos warband's spellcasting leader, he starts with one Seer Mark of Chaos of his choice, fitting the god he serves (a Carnival of Chaos may take only the Mark of Onogal, and so on). With the Eye of the Gods as well, he may still gain the Leader Mark, as a Marauders of Chaos Seer who became leader would.

rules.title: Gifted Servants
rules.text: A Chaos Hero who rolls a double on an advance that earns a new skill may instead roll a random mutation, or buy one. A model that already bears a Mark of Chaos may buy mutations from the Gifts of the Gods list instead.

rules.title: Mutant fugitives
rules.text:
What happens to a warrior who is not a Chaos worshipper when he gains a mutation (Corrupted Characters' Abominations, revised for this campaign). Skaven and Chaos Dwarfs embrace it, and nothing happens. A member of a religious warband (Sisters of Sigmar, Witch Hunters, Horned Hunters and the like) is put to death at once: remove the Hero and all his equipment.

Any other Hero faces his leader. Before the next battle the leader takes a Leadership test, at -1 for each mutant the warband already harbours. If it fails, the mutant stays, and no further test is needed unless he gains another mutation. If it passes, the mutant is expelled from the roster: roll a D6, and on a 5+ he seeks out his kin and may from then on be hired by Chaos warbands as a hired sword, for 20 gc plus twice his experience, with an upkeep of a third of that, rounded up.

rules.title: The Lure of Chaos
rules.text:
A Human warband may succumb to the Dark Gods. It must test when it has 3 or more Heroes with at least one mutation each, or 1 or more Heroes carrying 2 or more wyrdstone items (evaluated shards, tattoo ink, an eyeglass and the like) or at least 2 heretical books (a Tome of Magic, Book of the Dead, Tome of Daemonology, Grimoire of Dark Magic or Liber Chaotica).

Every Hero takes a Leadership test, those affected and those not, and the side with more successes wins; the leader's success counts as two. If the unaffected side wins, one affected Hero, picked at random, is thrown out of the warband as an example. If the affected side wins, the warband turns to Chaos: its alignment becomes Evil, and it may have to change plot, losing no Campaign Points for it. An unaffected leader is murdered: strike him from the roster and promote a new leader. An affected leader becomes a cult leader and executes one unaffected Hero, picked at random.

From then on the warband counts as a Chaos warband for every purpose, Branded by Chaos included. Its new leader may take the Eye of the Gods instead of his next skill, and a spellcaster a Seer Mark of Chaos.

battle_rules.title: Flying
battle_rules.text:
A model with the Fly special rule is either grounded or airborne; tokens help to show which.

Movement: it may move up to three times its Movement in any direction, ignoring terrain, and height climbed counts towards the distance. A model that flies is airborne, and is still airborne in the turn after.

Hard target: a model on the ground may charge an airborne model, but hits it in close combat only on a 6 to hit, unless it attacks with a spear. Until it is hit, the airborne model stays airborne, does not count as in combat, and may fly off or charge in its own turn. A flying model that charges is grounded.

Easy target: shooting at an airborne model is at +1 to hit, on top of any other modifiers, and a missile hit does not ground it.

Transports: boarding and leaving an airborne transport follow the rules for a moving cart, and a grounded one a stationary cart. A transport flies at its own fixed rate and does not triple it.

Mounts: a flying mount follows the Whoa Boy rules, except that a result of 3-4 while airborne gives the rider D3 hits at a Strength of half the distance it moved last turn.

A model flying on its own that is knocked down while airborne must pass D3 Initiative tests to land knocked down; if it fails, it takes D3 hits at a Strength of half the distance it moved last turn. A stunned flier takes these hits automatically.

battle_rules.title: Summoning daemons
battle_rules.text:
Only a wizard or spellcaster with the Chaos Rituals or a Chaos god's spell list may try to summon a daemon, and he may summon one per battle. The summoning materials cost 30 gc and are a common item for Chaos warbands. They are used up when the daemon appears, and only then: materials whose daemon never came carry over to the next battle. Holding them raises the warband's rating by 30 points, whether or not a daemon is summoned. A daemon keeps no upkeep, and must be summoned to each battle afresh.

Khorne hates magic and lets none of his daemons be summoned; they come only through a Warp Tear.

battle_rules.title: The summoning ritual
battle_rules.text:
First the wizard draws the summoning circle, in his movement phase: he may not move, and may not be in close combat, knocked down, stunned or otherwise hampered. One turn draws it; place a small blast template (3") beside him.

From the next turn, at the end of the movement phase, roll a dice for each friendly Hero in base contact with the circle, each captured warrior, henchman or sacrificial animal inside it, and each dice other rules add. Everyone taking part does nothing else that turn. A result on the Summoning results chart takes effect at once. The dice of a Summon or Warp Tear result may not be re-rolled, but the others may, to add to it: with three 3s, a 1 and a 4, re-roll the 1 or the 4 to try for four or five of a kind. With no result, the ritual may be tried again next turn.

After a Summon or a Warp Tear the circle is wiped, and every sacrifice inside it is killed and struck from its roster.

battle_rules.title: Daemons of Chaos
battle_rules.text:
Every daemon causes fear and has these rules.

Daemonic Flesh: a base armour save of 5+, modified by the Strength of the attack as normal and negated completely by magic weapons and spells. Its attacks count as magical, and it is immune to all poison and disease.

Daemon Mind: it is immune to all psychology and never takes a psychology test. If its warband routs, it dissolves back into the void.

Summoned Instability: every turn after the first it loses 1 Leadership and must pass a Leadership test, or it is pulled back into the warp. A greater daemon loses 3 a turn instead, and one that rolls a double 1 for the test has stabilised and stays for the rest of the game.

Mounts of the Gods: a beast daemon that is ridden, or pulls a cart or chariot, suffers no instability, and the warband that summoned it needs no Ride skill to ride it.

charts.title: Summoning results
charts.description: Read after rolling the summoning dice: the most dice showing the same number.
charts.note: The book prints the results on 1s in a column of their own, headed Warp Tear.

rows.name: Possessed
rows.text: A random warrior taking part gains +1 Wound, +1 Strength and +1 Attack. His attacks count as magic and he follows the rules for summoned instability, though his Leadership never drops below the one on his profile.

rows.name: Half summon
rows.text: The summoning works, but the daemon appears away from the circle: roll a scatter dice and 2D6, and it appears that far from the board edge the scatter dice shows.

rows.name: Summoned
rows.text: The summoning works as meant: place a lesser daemon, or daemons, of your god in the circle. They may move and act this turn.

rows.name: Greater summon
rows.text: A perfect summoning: place any daemon, greater daemons included, in the circle. It may move and act this turn.

rows.name: Feedback
rows.text: The summoners are thrown D6" backwards, taking a Strength 3 hit if they hit another model or a piece of terrain.

rows.name: Hostile summon
rows.text: Roll on the Warp Tear chart. The daemon rolled is summoned unbound: it appears in base contact with a random summoner and attacks him. It may be a greater daemon, or even the dramatis persona Oxyotl, which is the only way to bring him into the campaign.

rows.name: Punished!
rows.text: The angry gods turn a random Hero taking part into a daemonic steed, rolled at random from the beast daemons.

rows.name: Warp rift
rows.text: A hole is torn in reality: the circle grows 2D6" each turn, any model it touches is taken out of action and any terrain piece it covers completely is destroyed. Roll a D6 at the start of each round: on a 1 the rift collapses and is gone.

rows.name: Gift of the Gods
rows.text: The warband leader becomes a Daemon Prince, with the profile from Border Town Burning. If he ever rolls a double 6 on a Leadership test he is called back to the Realm of Chaos: strike him from the roster.

charts.title: Warp Tear
charts.description: Rolled for a hostile summon, and for a daemon that slips into the world through a warp tear: the D6 picks its kind, then roll on that kind's table.

rows.name: Beast daemon
rows.text: Roll a D6 on the beast daemons.

rows.name: Disc of Tzeentch
rows.text: The table calls it the Flying disc.

rows.name: Lesser daemons
rows.text: Roll a D6 on the lesser daemons.

rows.name: Greater daemon
rows.text: Roll 2D6 on the greater daemons.

rows.name: Oxyotl
rows.text: The dramatis persona, freed from the warp.

charts.title: Da Prophecy
charts.description: Da Prophet's prophecies for a warband following Da Waaagh: the first at 5 Campaign Points, each completed scoring D3.
charts.note: Re-roll a prophecy that can't be completed because that race or item isn't in the game. A Warboss who can't complete one after 3 games may go off alone to complete it in secret: he misses D3 games, swears on his return that he did it, and Da Prophet gives him his next.

rows.name: I see ya riding on...
rows.text: Roll on the Animal? table. The leader must learn to ride the animal rolled, find one, and ride it into battle.

rows.name: I see ya holding dat magical thing
rows.text: Roll on a random magical artefact table. The leader must acquire and use the artefact rolled.

rows.name: You'se sittin in...'s 'ouse, eatin'...
rows.text: Roll on the What? table, then the Who? table, then the Animal? table. The leader must take the encampment of the warrior rolled and eat the animal rolled.

rows.name: I seez ya snackin on a...
rows.text: Roll on the Animal? table. The leader must eat the animal rolled.

rows.name: I see da boss standin' over da broken body of...
rows.text: Roll on the What? table, then the Who? table, then the How? table. The leader must defeat the warrior rolled in the way rolled, and has the skill Taunt until the prophecy is done.

rows.name: Da greatest Green won az emerged victorias
rows.text: Roll on the Who? table, then on a scenario table. Defeat the enemy rolled in the scenario rolled.

rows.name: Da one who will be Gork (or Mork) haz grabbed da...
rows.text: Roll on the What? table, then the Who? table, then the With? table. Capture the enemy rolled and do with him what was rolled.

rows.name: Da ... was in da most troubles until da best boss saved 'im
rows.text: Roll on the Who? table twice. Ally with the warband first rolled against the enemy second rolled.

rows.name: Youse with ya 5 most trusted boyz
rows.text: Roll on a scenario table. Win the scenario rolled with 6 Heroes alive.

rows.name: Its da boss, he's on da ground, taken a beatin
rows.text: Roll on the Who? table, then on a scenario table. Lose the scenario rolled against the enemy rolled, with the Warboss out of action.

rows.name: Nah you ain't the chosen one
rows.text: Roll on the serious injury chart at once until a result of 16-35 comes up. The prophecy is fulfilled as soon as the injury is taken.

rows.name: Da Strongest
rows.text: The highest Strength.

rows.name: Da Weakest
rows.text: The lowest Toughness.

rows.name: Da Biggest
rows.text: The most Wounds.

rows.name: Da Oliest
rows.text: A priest, or the most serious injuries.

rows.name: Da Grossest
rows.text: The most mutations.

rows.name: Burstin with Magics
rows.text: A spellcaster or an artefact holder.

charts.title: Da Prophecy: Who?
charts.note: The book heads this table D6, but its results run from 2 to 12.

rows.name: Da vision was blurry
rows.text: It could 'ave been anyone: any race.

rows.name: Tall and Pointy one
rows.text: An Elf.

rows.name: Stuntie
rows.text: A Dwarf or Halfling.

rows.name: Rat man
rows.text: Skaven.

rows.name: Beast thing
rows.text: Beastmen.

rows.name: A Dirty Humie
rows.text: Human.

rows.name: A Greenie
rows.text: Greenskin.

rows.name: Scaly Boyz
rows.text: Lizardmen.

rows.name: Taint'd thing
rows.text: Chaos.

rows.name: Somethin Big!
rows.text: Large.

rows.name: Somethin Weird
rows.text: Anything else: Fimir, Dryads, ghosts, undead and the like.

rows.name: Atop the tallest thing in the land
Sacrifice to the bitz pile
rows.text: For D6 bitz.

charts.title: Da Prophecy: Animal?
charts.note: The book heads this table D6 but prints no 6: its results are 1 to 5 and 7.

rows.name: A Rat thing
rows.text: Roll on the Moulder Market chart.

rows.name: A Boring thing
rows.text: Roll on the speciality animals chart.

rows.name: A Fly'n thing
rows.text: Roll on the feathered friends chart.

rows.name: A lovely green thing
rows.text: Roll on the Greenskins animal chart.

rows.name: A jungle thing
rows.text: Roll on the Lustrian animal chart.

rows.name: Somethin random
rows.text: Roll on a random Seaside Situations monster chart.

locations.name: Battle Monks' Monastery
locations.rules: Only a Battle Monks warband may come here, instead of searching for rare items in the post-battle sequence. It may send one Hero to the monks to heal one permanent Serious Injury; he misses the next D3 battles.

location_groups.name: Da Camp
location_groups.description: The Waaagh's camp, its tents run by goblins. Where a place here speaks of the Waaagh level, it means the number of Campaign Point achievements the warband has reached, not its total Campaign Points.
location_groups.restrictions: Only a Greenskin warband following Da Waaagh, once it has reached 5 Campaign Points, and only its Greenskin Heroes, instead of searching for a rare item. No Hero of another race may visit.

locations.name: Gobbo Shaman Hut
locations.rules:
Magic Drinkz: for a donation of 5 gold crowns the shaman brews a potion for the warrior to drink before the next battle; once he has drunk it, roll on the Potions table (Herbalist), which the Annual prints again as Magic Drinkz.

Gubbinz: for 25 gold crowns the shaman sells a bag of bones and guts. A Greenskin shaman who eats it automatically passes 1 spell in the next game. Roll a D6, and the shaman has choked on the Gubbinz and is stunned (the book gives no score for this). After each game in which the Gubbinz were used, roll 2D6: on a 2 the shaman has turned for good into a giant Shamanshroom, and from then on the warband has unlimited Madcap Mushrooms and Gubbinz. Each time one is taken from the Shamanshroom roll a D6, and on a 1 it was the last and the Shamanshroom is lost.

Sneaky Spells: only once your Waaagh is at least 15 (so printed), pay 50 gold crowns and roll a D6 on the Sneaky Spells table.

tables.title: Sneaky Spells
tables.description: Rolled for each 50 gold crowns paid.

rows.name: Cursed
rows.text: A Goblin trick: the Hero is cursed instead, and a random characteristic drops by 1 for good.

rows.name: Hex
rows.text: The shaman curses a Hero of another warband, in the same way.

rows.name: Miracle
rows.text: He lifts any curse, heals any lost wounds, cures any mutation or removes a serious injury from a Hero of your choice.

locations.name: Shiny Bits Pile
locations.rules:
Heroes may give Treasures, gold or items to the pile, Treasures and items counting at their selling price. Each time something is given, roll 2D6: on a 2-3, D6 x 25 gold crowns' worth has gone missing from the pile. Nothing given may ever be taken back. As the pile grows, the warband gains each step of the Shiny Bits Pile table.

The Rogue Idol of Gork (or possibly Mork) may be used only while the pile holds at least 200 gold crowns and the warband's Waaagh achievement level is at least 4; the book prints no hire price. M 6, WS 3, BS 0, S *, T *, W *, I 2, A *, Ld 9, with a stone body and fists. Causes fear; Gigantic Creature; Cannot Run, though it may charge; Battle Lust: it must charge any enemy it can see. Spirit of the Waaaagh: its Wounds, Attacks, Strength and Toughness each equal the warband's Waaagh achievement level (5 with 25 Campaign Points, which is 5 achievements). Stone Body: a 4+ special save only hammers modify. Avalanche: when it is taken out of action, every model within 2" takes a Strength 4 hit. Made of Bitz: when it is taken out of action, the pile loses D6 x 10 gold. Livin' Idol: friendly models within 6" gain +1 Leadership and spellcasters may re-roll one dice per casting, but when it is taken out of action the whole warband is at -1 Leadership for the rest of the battle.

tables.title: Shiny Bits Pile
tables.description: What the warband gains as the gold in the pile grows.

rows.text: Henchmen cost 5 gold crowns less.
The warband may hire the Rogue Idol.
When recruiting Henchmen, add +1 to the experience available.
Henchmen die after a battle only on a 1, rather than 1-2.

locations.name: Da Zoo
locations.rules: A Greenskin visitor may take one of the animals hanging around, rolling 2D6 on the Da Zoo table, or order one: choose it and roll for its rarity; if it is not found, the handlers track it down, and each later visit adds +1 to the rarity roll. A warrior of the warband with the animal handling skill for the beast may miss the next battle to help find it, and it is yours when he returns, the price still paid.

tables.title: Da Zoo
tables.description: Rolled for what is hanging around the pens.

rows.name: Giant Squig
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 14, 250 gold crowns. M 3D6, WS 4, BS 0, S 5, T 5, W 3, I 4, A 3, Ld 5 (printed Great Squig). No weapons or armour. Moves as a Cave Squig on 3D6. Wild: without a Goblin within 6" at the start of its move it goes wild, moving 2D6" in a random direction each turn, towards the nearest model it can see on a hit, and fighting any model it touches, its own side's too; it is out of your control for the rest of the game. Causes fear. Large Target. An animal: gains no experience. Monstrous Mount: +20 to the warband rating; shots at its rider hit the mount on 1-4 and the rider on 5-6, in close combat attackers choose, and the usual +1 armour for a mount applies. Skull of Iron: stunned counts as knocked down. Staggered, but not down: each knocked down result costs it 1 Attack until its next recovery phase.

rows.name: Gore-Grunta
rows.text: Rare 12, 150 gold crowns. M 8, WS 3, BS 0, S 5, T 4, W 2, I 3, A 1, Ld 3. Tusks and bulk, unarmed without penalty. Thunderous Charge: a rider charging over 7" causes D3 impact hits at the grunta's Strength. Thick Skinned: +1 more to the rider's armour save (+2 in all).

rows.name: Cave Squig
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 10, 40 gold crowns. M 2D6, WS 4, BS 0, S 4, T 3, W 1, I 4, A 1, Ld 5. No weapons or armour. Movement: it moves 2D6", never runs or declares charges, and counts as charging if that move reaches an enemy. Minderz: it must stay within 6" of a Goblin, or goes wild as the Giant Squig does. Just Squigs: it counts as half a model for Rout tests. An animal: gains no experience.

rows.name: Giant Wolf
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 10, 85 gold crowns. M 9, WS 3, BS 0, S 3, T 3, W 1, I 4, A 1, Ld 4. Fangs and claws, unarmed without penalty. An animal: gains no experience. Territorial: not in a warband that already has Giant Spiders.

rows.name: Squig Wig
rows.text: Rare 7, 30 gold crowns. An extra 6+ special save after other armour saves; when it saves, the wig rolls for out of action as a Henchman does. On a 4+ the wearer may ignore a Madness or Blinded in one eye Serious Injury, the wig dying instead, but he is at -1 Leadership in the next battle from embarrassment. A new wig must then be bought.

rows.name: Droppinz
rows.text: Goblins and Savage Orcs only, Rare 7, 25 gold crowns. One use: a Goblin or Savage Orc Hero takes a Leadership test before the battle to coat himself, and anyone who wants to strike him must pass a Leadership test in the first round of combat or be at -1 to hit that round.

rows.name: War Boar
rows.text: Orcs only, Rare 11, 90 gold crowns. M 7, WS 3, BS 0, S 3, T 4, W 1, I 3, A 1, Ld 3. Ferocious Charge: the boar, not its rider, has +2 Strength when charging. Thick Skinned: +1 more to the rider's armour save (+2 in all).

rows.name: Giant Spider
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 11, 100 gold crowns. M 7, WS 3, BS 0, S 3/4, T 3, W 1, I 4, A 1, Ld 4. Poisoned Attack: it attacks at Strength 4, without changing armour saves. Wall Walk: it and its rider climb walls with no Initiative test, and may jump only 2" across or down, which counts as a diving charge; the rider tests Initiative on a jump, and on a failure rolls on the Whoa Boy! table; even with Running Dismount the diving charge is at most 2". Not in a warband that already has Giant Wolves.

rows.name: Mangler Squig
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 13, 200 gold crowns. M 2D6, WS 3, BS 0, S 5, T 4, W 3, I 3, A D6+1, Ld 5. Ker-splat!: a double on its charge roll gives +1 to hit until the end of the turn. Watch Out!: when slain, roll a dice for each unit within 3", friend or foe, and on a 4+ it suffers a wound. Wild, fear, Large Target, animal, Monstrous Mount (+20 rating), Skull of Iron, Staggered but not down and Movement, all as the Giant Squig and Cave Squig.

rows.name: Gigantic Spider
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 13, 200 gold crowns. M 6, WS 3, BS 0, S 5, T 5, W 3, I 4, A 2, Ld 4. No weapons or armour. Causes fear. Large Monster: it may always be shot at. Poisonous: on the injury roll for a wound it causes, 1 is knocked down, 2-4 stunned, 5-6 out of action. Native: no penalty in woods. Non-sentient: subject to stupidity, gains no experience, and may climb.

locations.name: Goblin Tinkerer
locations.rules: A Greenskin visitor may take a weapon already made, rolling a D6 on the Goblin Tinkerer table, or order one: choose it and roll for its rarity; if it is not found the tinkerers start work, and each later visit adds +1 to the rarity roll. A Hero may have only one order at a time; a new order stops work on the old one.

tables.title: Goblin Tinkerer
tables.description: Rolled for what the tinkerer has on offer.

rows.name: Doom Diver
rows.text: Rare 12, 150 gold crowns. M 3, T 7, W 3 (the rest printed as dashes). Cannot run; Large Target. Gobbo Operated: a crew of two Goblins, one with the Artillery Expert skill. Reload: the crew spends a full turn readying the goblin (mark it loaded) and fires in a later turn. Pegged Down: it cannot fire in a turn it moved. Glidin Gob: a volunteer goblin in contact with it the turn before is launched the artillery dice's score; he may fly straight into a target, or otherwise counts as Flying, moving on the artillery dice each turn. SPLAAAT: after rolling his move he may steer into a warrior, vehicle or building, taking and dealing D3 hits at a Strength equal to the dice; taken out of action this way he rolls twice on the serious injury table and, if he lives, gains 3 experience. Misfire: on a misfire in the turn he is fired, roll on the Doom Diver Misfire table; a misfire while flying means falling from the sky (flying rules).

chart.title: Doom Diver Misfire
chart.description: Rolled on a misfire in the turn the goblin is fired.

rows.text: The catapult leaps into the air and crashes down, destroying itself and taking the goblin out of action.
It spins on the spot while the crew run for cover: they are too dizzy to launch this turn or next.
It tips over and fires the goblin face first into the ground: he is out of action and rolls twice on the serious injury table.
The Doom Diver flies straight up out of sight, and rejoins the warband after the battle from somewhere far away.
Crew and ammo argue about whose go it is: no Doom Diver is fired this turn.

He is fired along the ground, ploughing 3D6" in a straight line and hitting any unit in his way as normal, through more than one model; if he hits terrain he is out of action and rolls twice on the injury chart.

rows.name: Spear Chukka
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 9, 90 gold crowns. Range 36", Strength 5. Multiple Wounds (D2). Hard to Fire: a crew, one with Weapons Training and at least one a goblin; it fires every second turn with 2 crew and every turn with 4. Save Modifier: a further -1 (-3 in all). Move or Fire; Prepare Shot. Penetrate Ranks, as the Bolt Thrower (Artillery Weapons, Cartwright). Misfire: on a to hit roll of 1, roll on the Spear Chukka Misfire table.

chart.title: Spear Chukka Misfire
chart.description: Rolled on a to hit roll of 1.

rows.text: The string snaps: every goblin crewing it is out of action, and the chukka is destroyed.
It fires early with a goblin reloading it: both goblin and spear hit the target, harming both.
The spear jams: it cannot fire this turn or next.
Nobody loaded it: it fires next turn as normal.
The spear flies wild: roll a scatter dice and shoot it the full 36" that way, hitting whatever it meets.
It fires with too much force, causing D6 wounds instead of D2.

rows.name: Rock Lobba
rows.text: Rare 12, 200 gold crowns. M 3, T 6, W 3, Ld 6. Range 12"-48". Hard to Fire: it fires every other turn with two crew and every turn with four, never moving and firing in one turn, and no Shooting skills apply. Large Target. Constructed: it starts as 4 small crates any models may carry, though only goblins work it, and takes D3 turns to set up; once up it may only swivel, and taking it down takes 1 turn. Artillery: name the landing spot, line of sight not needed, and roll the scatter and artillery dice; it lands off target by the scatter dice's number less the crew's Ballistic Skill, a hit being a direct hit. Indirect Fire: without line of sight a hit still veers, in the small arrow's direction, by the artillery dice less the crew's Ballistic Skill. Explosive Radius: the model under the centre of the small blast template takes a Strength 6 hit, every other model under it Strength 5. Misfire: on the artillery dice, roll on the Rock Lobba Misfire table.

chart.title: Rock Lobba Misfire
chart.description: Rolled on a misfire on the artillery dice.

rows.name: DESTROYED!
rows.text: It breaks apart: every crewman must pass an Initiative test or be crushed and taken out of action, and the lobba is destroyed.

rows.name: Disabled.
rows.text: It suffers a wound, healed only by taking it apart and rebuilding it, and cannot fire this turn or next.

rows.name: May Not Shoot.
rows.text: A small error: it may not fire this turn.

rows.name: Stabba Lobba
rows.text: Savage Orcs only, Rare 12, 90 gold crowns. Range 48", Strength 7. Multiple Wounds (D3). Livin' Artillery: 4 orcs work it, two holding the bow and two drawing it. Save Modifier: a further -1 (-3 in all). Move or Fire; Prepare Shot. Penetrate Ranks, as the Bolt Thrower (Artillery Weapons, Cartwright).

rows.name: Chariot
rows.text: Rare 12, 100 gold crowns plus steeds. Any fitting greenskin steeds may be bought with it, but not squigs.

rows.name: Squig Gobba
rows.text: Goblins only, Rare 14, 150 gold crowns. M 3, T 4, W 3, I 2, Ld 6. Range 8"-36", Strength 4 or special. Large Target. Gobbo Operated and Reload, as the Doom Diver. Spittin' Beast: it cannot run or charge, nor fire in a turn it moved. Bounce: as the Carronade (Artillery Weapons, Cartwright), with a squig for the cannonball. Misfire!: on the first artillery dice it rolls about spewing; every model within 2" takes a Strength 4 hit and the Gobba is knocked down. Livin' Ammo: any squig in base contact may be loaded. A raw squig hits at Strength 4 and bounces on; after its last hit it lands on its feet, counting as charging, if it passes an Initiative test, and otherwise rolls on the Injury table. A squig loaded with shrooms may be set off by its handlers any time after its first impact, wounding every model under a small blast template on a 3+, and is lost.

locations.name: Snotling Corna
locations.rules: In the Snotling Corner (so its text calls it) Greenskin Heroes try impressive feats to win a snotling's service: pass the test on the Snotling Corna table and pay its price. Each Greenskin may have at most 2 snotlings at a time. When the Hero is taken out of action roll a D6: on a 1-3 his snotling has died and a new one must be won. The Snotling Horde is printed among them, and presumably hired here.

tables.title: Snotling Corna
tables.description: The snotlings on offer and the feat each needs.

rows.text: 20 gold crowns, on a passed Strength test. One extra Strength 1 attack, made with the Hero's and at his target, that ignores armour saves.
15 gold crowns, on a passed Initiative test. The Hero may re-roll 1 dice on the exploration chart.
40 gold crowns, on a passed Leadership test. The Hero gains +1 to rarity rolls.

10 gold crowns times the Waaagh level. M 4, WS 2, BS 0, S 1, T 1, W *, I 3, A *, Ld 5+*, armed with sharp stuff. Mob mentality: its Wounds, Attacks and Leadership bonus equal the Waaagh achievement level (a warband with 25 Waaagh has 5 W, 5 A and 10 Ld). Horde: a warband may hire as many hordes as its Waaagh achievement level, counting towards its most warriors. Overwhelm: charging, it may give up any number of Attacks for +1 Strength each.

locations.name: Da Bash Tent
locations.rules:
It is best to keep track of a Hero's wins in his notes.

The Hero fights the opponent the Da Bash Tent table gives for his wins so far; compare Initiative to see which side charges. If he loses he rolls on the Serious Injuries table but keeps his equipment, and if he lives he returns to his warband. If he wins he earns 50 gold crowns and +2 experience. A Large model must start against the 2 Orc Boys. Note each fight a warrior wins.

A Hero who has won 10 fights is a legend of Da Tent and may fight no more bouts, because nobody will bet on his opponents.

tables.title: Da Bash Tent
tables.description: The opponent a returning Hero faces, by the fights he has won.
tables.note: Beating the opponents for 6 to 9 wins earns a further +1 experience and +25 gold crowns; your leader may take +1 Campaign Point instead. The book names the Custom Weapons chart but does not print it.

rows.text: Two Goblins armed with spears.
An Orc Boy with two choppas.
Four Goblins with spears.
Two Orc Boys.
A Black Orc with two choppas, heavy armour and the Pit Fighter skill.
A Squig Herder with a prodda and 2 squigs. A Hero who beats them gains frenzy.
Two Black Orcs with two choppas, heavy armour and the Pit Fighter skill, that win the charge.
A Troll.
A Troll and two Fanatics.
Two Mangler Squigs.

After 9 wins, the next challenge is two Mangler Squigs and two Trolls. A win pays a purse of 250 gold crowns and a further D3 experience; roll twice on the Custom Weapons chart and give him the weapon of his choice of the two.
